newsitem.title: CANADA: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE WILL CONTINUE TO SPEAK OUT.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE WILL CONTINUE TO SPEAK OUT.

text.p: Jacques Villeneuve will continue to speak his mind despite his reprimand by Formula One bosses.

The Canadian arrived in Montreal on Thursday after his ticking off by the International Automobile Federation in Paris the previous day and said: "I've not been asked to change my views or to stop expressing them. But I have to change the way in which I put them in words.

"I know now that you cannot use the language you would use at home when you are talking to the international media, but I knew that for some time. I know I can't say things any more like the regulations are stupid, or anything like that."

The Williams driver, called before the FIA after he ridiculed its plans for grooved tyres and narrower cars next season, explained that from now on he would avoid climbing out of his car and speaking when he felt excited.
He said: "I realise now, I will have to take a deep breath, think more slowly and consider the words I am using."

Asked if he would continue to criticise when he felt he had to, he replied: "Yes, definitely. I will still say what I think. It may not be that I am thinking in the same way as other people, but if I have something to say, I will still say it."
He explained that he felt it was important for him to criticise next year's regulations because he felt they would take all the pleasure out of racing.

Asked about the need for him to have flown back to Paris only two days before opening practice for his home Canadian Grand Prix this weekend, he said he would have preferred the FIA World Council to have dealt with the matter a week earlier or a week later.
"That would have been much better," he said. "These comments came out a long time ago and Mr Mosley (FIA president) spoke to me about them at the drivers' briefing in Monaco."
